quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Genealogy Requirement 1, what is the difference between a primary genealogical source and a secondary source when researching your family's pedigree chart?
quiz_item.question: In Genealogy Requirement 1, what is the difference between a primary genealogical source and a secondary source when researching your family's pedigree chart?
options: A. A primary source is an original record created at or near the time of the event by a direct participant or official witness (such as an original birth certificate, parish baptismal register, or contemporaneous ship manifest), whereas a secondary source is compiled later from other accounts (such as a published county history or an unsourced online family tree).
B. A primary source is any story repeated at a family reunion fifty years later, whereas a secondary source is a courthouse marriage license signed by the officiating judge.
C. A primary source refers only to relatives on your father's side, whereas a secondary source refers to relatives on your mother's side.
D. Secondary sources are always 100 percent error-free and never need to be verified against vital records or federal census schedules.
